LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.NotScanned: The scan has not run yet. Restart RimWorld with Joy Rescue enabled.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.NothingToRescue: Every recreation building in your modlist is already served by a recreation giver. Nothing to fix.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.Summary: {0} buildings, {1} usable, {2} orphaned, {3} rescued, {4} types you can actually get
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.SummaryTip:
The {0} types come from buildings a colonist can actually use.
Expectations ask for up to six different ones, and tolerance is counted per type: ten chess tables still count as one.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RescueModsWithOwnCode: Also rescue buildings from mods that ship their own recreation code

Those mods define their own recreation givers or job drivers, so they may already handle the building in code without listing it in a giver. Rescuing them anyway can produce two competing jobs on the same building. Left off, they are still listed below and can be enabled one by one.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RequireChair: Watching requires a chair or a bed
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RequireChairTip: On: the base game behaviour for televisions — no seat in range, no watching. Off: colonists watch standing up, which keeps a rescued screen from sitting unused for want of a chair. Only affects buildings set to "watch".
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.SortModeTip:
Click to cycle.
By state: whatever needs attention comes first - dead types, then types with an orphan, then the ones already served. Most furniture first: shows at a glance where you are rich and where you are thin. A type with one building is one bad day from being useless. By name: for finding something you already know the name of.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.LogReportDone: Joy Rescue report written to the log.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.ConfirmReset: Restore every Joy Rescue setting to its default?
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RowTipOwnCode: This mod defines recreation givers or job drivers of its own. It may already handle this building in code. Enable only if colonists visibly never use it.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.NoJoyBuildings: No recreation building at all was found in this modlist.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RowTipCovered: Already served by its own mod. Nothing to fix, and nothing to switch off here.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.RowTipOrphan: No activity points at this building. Left alone, no colonist would ever use it.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindHeaderDead: {0} — NO activity at all: this type is unreachable and counts for nothing
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindHeaderBroken: {0} — {1} building(s), {2} of them orphaned and waiting to be rescued
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindHeaderNoBuilding: {0} — no building, {1} activity/activities: comes from items or actions
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindHeaderOff: {0} — switched off by you: its {1} activity/activities are held at zero and it counts for nothing until you switch it back on
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindTipNeedsThing: Needs an object or a building. Without one, a colonist cannot take this recreation at all.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindTipNoThing: Needs no object: a colonist does this on their own, anywhere.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindTipWhatIsActivity: An "activity" is a way of taking that recreation: playing chess, watching television. One activity can serve several pieces of furniture, and furniture no activity points at is furniture nobody uses.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.GiverTipMove: Moving an activity moves its job and every building it serves, all at once. That is on purpose: the game credits the recreation type of the JOB, and logs an error if a building disagrees with it. Nothing here can be half-moved.
LanguageData.JoyRescue.Settings.KindTipTolerance: Tolerance is counted per type, not per building: a colonist who has played chess all week is just as tired of poker. Expectations ask for up to six different types, so a new type is worth more than a tenth building of an old one.
